# MCP and RAG Servers: References

Always prefer the current MCP specification and each product's current documentation. The specification
changes between dated revisions (2026-07-28 removed sessions and the initialize handshake). Re-verify links
and contents when updating this skill.

Last verified: 2026-10-30

## Specification and vendor (authoritative)

- MCP specification
  - Versioning (lists the current revision): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning
  - Security best practices (confused deputy, token passthrough, SSRF, state handle hijacking, local server
    compromise, scope minimization):
    https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/security_best_practices
  - Authorization (OAuth 2.1, protected resource metadata, resource indicators):
    https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization
  - Streamable HTTP transport (Origin validation, localhost binding, authentication):
    https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http
  - Tools (human in the loop, untrusted annotations, security considerations):
    https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools
  - Changelog for 2026-07-28: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog
  - Previous revision, for servers still on it (sessions, initialize handshake):
    https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports
- MCP Registry (metadata about published servers, not a security review): https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/
- MCP Inspector environment variables (ports, API token, bind and origin settings, secret storage):
  https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/blob/main/docs/environment-variables.md
- MCP Python SDK (transport security settings for Host and Origin checks):
  https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk
- Qdrant
  - Security (API keys, read-only keys, JWT RBAC, TLS, binding): https://qdrant.tech/documentation/security/
  - Security advisories: https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/security/advisories
- Chroma
  - Documentation: https://docs.trychroma.com/
  - Cookbook, authentication notes by version: https://cookbook.chromadb.dev/security/legacy-auth/
  - Security advisories: https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/security/advisories

Generic vulnerability and incident sources (CISA KEV, NVD, CVE, CISA ransomware guidance, IC3) are listed in
the core documents.

## Third-party (not authoritative)

- OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025): https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/
  Names the risk classes this skill uses (prompt injection, excessive agency, vector and embedding
  weaknesses, data poisoning). Doesn't describe MCP mechanics.
- Invariant Labs, tool poisoning attacks:
  https://invariantlabs.ai/blog/mcp-security-notification-tool-poisoning-attacks
  The research that named tool poisoning and "rug pull" changes. It's useful for understanding the attack;
  check its mitigation advice against current client features.
